steps.tx: Glucocorticoids rapidly diffuse across cell membranes to bind intracellular glucocorticoid receptors. **Transrepression** occurs when ligand-activated monomeric receptors bind proinflammatory transcription factors **NF-kappa-B** and **AP-1**, shutting down transcription of inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and inducible COX-2, producing potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects.
steps.say: Glucocorticoids act via transrepression, binding cytosolic receptors that directly inhibit NF-kappa-B and AP-1. This shuts down transcription of inflammatory cytokines and enzymes.

vis.alt: Glucocorticoid receptor binding and transcriptional repression of NF-kappa-B
vis.caption: Glucocorticoids inhibit inflammatory gene transcription via transrepression of NF-kappa-B. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: In contrast, **transactivation** involves receptor homodimers binding **glucocorticoid response elements** on genomic DNA, driving transcription of anti-inflammatory proteins such as annexin A1. Crucially, transactivation also drives the major metabolic toxicities of steroid therapy, including gluconeogenic enzymes causing hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and muscle wasting.
steps.say: Transactivation involves receptor homodimers binding DNA glucocorticoid response elements. While transactivation drives anti-inflammatory annexin, it also causes metabolic toxicities.

left.title: Transrepression (Anti-inflammatory)
points: Monomeric receptor binds NF-kappa-B and AP-1
Suppresses IL-1, IL-6, TNF, and COX-2

steps.tx: Very high pharmacological concentrations of glucocorticoids exert **rapid non-genomic effects** within seconds to minutes, independent of de novo gene transcription. Non-genomic mechanisms involve physicochemical intercalation into cellular and mitochondrial plasma membranes, rapidly altering calcium fluxes, dampening lymphocyte activation cascades, and reversing severe vascular permeability.
steps.say: High glucocorticoid doses exert rapid non-genomic actions within seconds to minutes. Intercalation into cell membranes modulates calcium fluxes and halts leukocyte activation.

nodes.label: Direct intercalation into mitochondrial and plasma membranes
Rapid dampening of intracellular calcium fluxes and leukocyte arrest

steps.tx: Relative anti-inflammatory potencies and mineralocorticoid properties vary widely: **hydrocortisone** possesses equivalent glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid activity (potency 1, mineralocorticoid 1); **prednisone** has **4-fold glucocorticoid potency** with minimal mineralocorticoid effect; **dexamethasone** possesses **25- to 30-fold potency** with zero mineralocorticoid effect, making it ideal for cerebral edema.
steps.say: Relative potencies vary significantly: hydrocortisone has potency of 1, prednisone has 4-fold anti-inflammatory potency, and dexamethasone exhibits 25- to 30-fold potency.

steps.tx: Intravenous pulse therapy with **methylprednisolone at 500 to 1,000 mg daily for 3 consecutive days** delivers immediate life-saving immunosuppression in rheumatologic emergencies. Clinical indications include acute diffuse alveolar hemorrhage in vasculitis, catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome, severe lupus nephritis, and giant cell arteritis with visual loss.
steps.say: Intravenous pulse methylprednisolone at 500 to 1,000 mg daily for 3 days treats rheumatologic emergencies, including alveolar hemorrhage, catastrophic APS, and acute visual loss in GCA.

nodes.label: Pulse IV methylprednisolone 500 to 1,000 mg over 60 minutes daily x 3 days
Cardiac telemetry monitoring to prevent malignant arrhythmias and sudden death

steps.tx: Therapy with prednisone exceeding **5 mg daily for 3 or more months** causes rapid trabecular bone loss, producing **glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis**. Fractures characteristically occur at significantly **higher bone mineral density T-scores** than postmenopausal osteoporosis; oral bisphosphonates are strongly recommended for patients at moderate-to-high fracture risk.
steps.say: Prednisone over 5 mg daily for 3 months triggers glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis. Fractures occur at higher T-scores, warranting oral bisphosphonate prophylaxis.

left.title: Glucocorticoid osteoporosis
points: Accelerated early bone loss in first 3 to 6 months
Vertebral fractures occur at normal/osteopenic T-scores

right.title: Prophylactic management
points: Daily calcium (1,000-1,200 mg) and vitamin D (800-2,000 IU)
Teriparatide for very high fracture risk

steps.tx: Sustained therapy suppresses the **hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis**, with suppression universally expected after **prednisone of 20 mg or more daily for greater than 3 weeks**. Abrupt cessation precipitates life-threatening **adrenal crisis**; patients undergoing major surgery or severe physiologic stress require intravenous **stress-dose hydrocortisone**.
steps.say: HPA axis suppression develops after prednisone over 20 mg daily for 3 weeks. Abrupt withdrawal triggers adrenal crisis, requiring stress-dose hydrocortisone during acute illness.

nodes.label: Exogenous prednisone >20 mg/day suppresses hypothalamic CRH and pituitary ACTH
Bilateral adrenal cortex atrophy and impaired endogenous cortisol reserves
Surgical stress without supplemental hydrocortisone triggers acute circulatory collapse

steps.tx: Long-term steroid-induced adverse effects include metabolic syndrome with steroid-induced diabetes, avascular osteonecrosis, posterior subcapsular cataracts, glaucoma, and opportunistic infections. Patients receiving **prednisone of 20 mg or more daily for over 4 weeks** combined with other immunosuppressants require **Pneumocystis jirovecii prophylaxis** with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
steps.say: Adverse effects include avascular necrosis, posterior subcapsular cataracts, and diabetes. Prednisone over 20 mg daily for 4 weeks warrants Pneumocystis prophylaxis.

rows: MRI screening for unexplained groin or knee pain
Annual slit-lamp exam and intraocular tonometry
